statement: Because the aid was project- and site-specific, the 2024 pause was functionally a cancellation: restarting required a fresh notification and a fresh Intel commitment, so the option was worth less than it appeared.
mechanism: State aid approved for a named project at a named site does not travel. Any re-scoped use needs a new Commission notification and a new member-state decision, each taking months and each a fresh political fight. A two-year pause therefore does not preserve the option; it destroys the approval that made the option valuable, while leaving Intel holding land costs and political expectations. Rational actors who understand this do not pause - they cancel, which is what happened a year later. Weakest link: whether the approval in fact lapsed or could be revived by administrative act; the aid decision text was not retrieved.

scope.where: EU state aid procedure for the Magdeburg project

relation_to_others.note: Explains why deferral was not a real option, reinforcing the cash story
Both locate the decisive constraint in institutions rather than demand
